# DrawingML luminance precision

Original OPC/XML swatches generated by
`tools/drawing_luminance_precision_fixture.py`, reusing this repository's own
anchor and theme fixtures. No corpus XML, artwork or fonts are redistributed.
The generator uses standard-library ZIP/JSON and permissively licensed lxml.

The 96 controls cover seven literal RGB colors and explicit theme white, each
with no transform, luminance modulation at 0/25/50/75/100%, positive and negative
luminance offsets, both orders of a modulation/offset pair, and saturation
modulation. Three pages contain 32 swatches each. The final source includes an
explicit theme; the preliminary theme-less capture was discarded and recaptured.

The reference application exported `native.pdf` from the exact source hash recorded
in `reference.json`. `tools/record_drawing_luminance_precision.py` records
nine interior samples per swatch and requires their colors to agree. Source
document, supported shape extension and theme pass schemas. Strict app import
produces 96 shape scenes.

Before the correction, the renderer matched 84/96 native swatches. White with 50%
luminance became 7F7F7F in the reference application and 808080 in the app. PDF operators independently
encode that native gray as 0.498, so the discrepancy is not simply antialiasing
or rasterizer rounding of a PDF 0.5 value. Other mismatches require a channel to
increase rather than decrease: 112233 at 25% luminance is 04090D in the reference application and
04080D in the former renderer. A blanket truncation cannot correct the conversion.
Experimental sRGB/linear round trips explain at most 89/96 controls and were
not installed. Gamma-2.2 round trips do not improve the 84/96 result.

Input/output quantization in linear RGB, to the nearest 1/100000 unit, now
matches all 96 cases. Intermediate transforms keep floating-point precision.
The independent `drawing-color-sequences` set adds 96 new cases and identifies
the correct quantization boundaries. Run
`node tools/check-drawing-luminance-precision.mjs` for the passing native check.
Unit and browser regressions verify the complete matrix, native painted pixels,
editing, exact undo and reopening. This is not a claim that every color feature
in OOXML is supported.

Relevant standard: ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.2.3.20–21 (`lumMod`, `lumOff`), plus
the color-model/transform definitions. The standard describes lightness
modulation and offset; the controls establish the conversion precision used by
the supported reader. No normative contradiction is claimed.
The published MS-OE376 [luminance-modulation implementation note](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oe376/d73682e1-10c0-4ddd-9835-664041f4f249)
does not supply a rounding algorithm. This DrawingML gap is tracked separately
from the still-unresolved WordprocessingML themeTint/themeShade precision.

## Neutral conversion-stage controls

`neutral-stages.docx` is a separately authored 32-swatch control using this
fixture's original shape/page scaffolding. Its four rows encode the same
neutral values as white plus `lumMod`, black plus `lumOff`, direct `hslClr`
(zero hue/saturation), and literal `srgbClr`. Values are 0, 1, 25000, 49999,
50000, 50001, 75000 and 100000 in percentage units; the literal row uses the
nearest RGB byte. The source passes the transitional and supported shape
schemas. Fresh reference output is `neutral-stages-native.pdf`.

The first three rows all produce gray bytes 0, 0, 64, 127, **127**, 128, 191,
255. The literal row instead preserves 128 at the central value. Thus the
half-gray behavior also occurs with direct HSL: it is not peculiar to either
luminance modifier, nor does the reference application globally change literal RGB 128 to 127.
These observations narrow the unresolved HSL conversion/quantization stage;
they do not establish its algorithm. Direct `hslClr` is not yet supported by
the app's drawing-color reader; this native-only diagnostic is not a claim of
new renderer support or a passing engine comparison.

`neutral-stages-reference.json` records exact source/PDF hashes, sample
coordinates and RGB arrays. Each native swatch was sampled at its center and
at all eight combinations of +/-10pt offsets; all nine samples must agree.

`neutral-boundaries.docx` broadens this to 64 swatches, checking values one unit
below, exactly at, and one unit above 10%, 30%, 50%, 70% and 90%, plus 100%.
All three HSL paths agree. The central byte values are 25, 77, 127, 179 and 229;
10.001% still yields 25. These observations disprove both ordinary byte rounding
and a universal ties-down rule, and are explained by the linear percentage
quantization. Its fresh native PDF, hashes and nine-sample RGB values are in
the corresponding `neutral-boundaries-*` files. Supported sRGB modifier paths
are covered by unit tests; direct HSL remains native-only diagnostic evidence.
